call_sites: reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:4739 (the admission pass loop that calls admit_once)

0.reason: the base arm's log header lost its file list; the head arm's log carries all 57 paths and the summary counts are recorded

findings.text: non-blocking: the base arm's `# command:` line reads `... -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q -n 6 56` and its `# files:` line (6) reads `56` where the file list belongs, so the log does not carry the literal command that produced its 393 passed/3 failed summary; the head arm's log at the same path family does carry all 57 paths. The done-when requires every log to carry its revision and the literal command, and the reviewed run's manifest repeats the defect as an unsubstituted `<every test file importing reckon.crew.queue_admission, 57 files> <...>` placeholder in `tests:` (manifest.md:11) and in `baseline_suite.command` (manifest.md:15), neither of which `crew check --manifest` refuses. The population is still reconstructible from the head arm's 57 files minus the new test file, and 396 = 399 - 3 reconciles, so the measurement stands and only its re-runnability is lost.

non-blocking: the attempt-resulted case creates its exit record at line 268 before the pass starts and hands `_after_the_pass_reads_the_queue` a no-op change (`lambda: None`), so its `assert fired` proves only that the pass read the queue; a guard that checked attempts once at pass start rather than immediately before the launch would pass this case too, leaving the plan's "the change written after the pass read the request as queued" requirement untested for the attempt read. The pointer case at line 250 does exercise the window, and the refusal itself is guarded (the attempt-read negative control reddens this case).

non-blocking: the fragment states that each case writes its change after the pass has read the request and that `fired` means "a case cannot pass by never applying its change", which is not true of the attempt-resulted case, whose record is written before the pass and whose hook applies nothing.

non-blocking: `_record_stalls` skips a request whose last verdict is already the stall or a hold, but a request the new guard refuses now has two rows in one pass record — `refused-before-launch` (4350) appended in the loop, then `stalled` appended afterwards — and `_last_verdict_of` returns the first matching row, so on the next pass it reads the refusal, does not skip, and appends a fresh stall row every pass. A permanently refused queued request (an attempt that already resulted) therefore breaks the module's documented "a wait that spans many passes yields one stall rather than one per pass"; the effect is bounded by the verdict log's trim and obligations dedupe by run id.
